tracks.narration: Before classifying any extremum, you have to find it. Where is the gradient zero?
Here is a function with hills and valleys: f equals x cubed over three, minus x, plus y squared, minus two y. The gradient field shows the uphill direction at every point.
Sweep a scanner across the line y equals one. The magnitude of the gradient drops to zero at exactly two places — x equals minus one and x equals plus one.
Solve the system: set ∇f equal to zero. The first component gives x squared equals one, so x is plus or minus one. The second gives y equals one. Two critical points fall out.
Critical points are zeros of the gradient. Find them first, then classify.
